`MobilityPolicy.Point` validates finite bounded coordinates/dimension. `Actor` carries stable world/principal/citizen/entity identity, generation and control revision from the trusted owner. `Limits` intersects all independent D caps; remaining allowance and absolute owner deadline can tighten an active session. `Goal` copies at most eight candidates and captures one immutable COME point. `Session.advance(Facts,navigationDone)` is externally clocked and returns MOVING, PROPOSE_ROUTE, ARRIVED or a typed BLOCKED observation. Same-tick calls are inert; earlier clocks, exhausted travel/deadline, unknown load/collision/control stop. `MobilityObservation` includes actual cumulative distance, elapsed ticks and last physical progress; it contains no integrated root or save receipt.

`MinecraftNavigationAdapter(ServerLevel,Mob,Authority)` installs nothing. Authority must freshly return `Control(identity,authorized,remaining,deadline)` from A's existing exclusive movement owner. Native entity UUID, dimension and feet are independently checked. `come(Actor,ServerPlayer)` captures actual server player feet. `storage(Actor,Scope,StorageResolver.Bound,Permission,MinecraftStorageAdapter)` requires the already-resolved opaque endpoint and a fresh native eligibility decision. It retains UUID/generation/epoch/topology and never repeats a name lookup. Fresh D05 checks preserve deposit-only privacy. `Route.step()` must run once each native server tick under that same A owner; `cancel()` stops only the route's own native Path. The adapter never ticks citizens itself, calls private NavigationRoute, acquires Jobs, adds chunk tickets or changes an actor position.

J02 maps the existing A root/custody/allowance context into Authority, keeps one movement executor, intersects remaining root budget/deadline, charges observed displacement and elapsed time to that original root, revalidates before invoking this port and cancels on control loss. It must not create an independent action root or treat decoded MobilityGoal/ALLOW bytes as capability. An authority observation change across the final native call boundary refuses movement. J01 supplies current loaded storage identity/access projections; J04 supplies authenticated production input. These adapters are deferred, not stubbed as successful integrations.

Public pinned 26.3 APIs used: Mob.getNavigation, PathNavigation.createPath(BlockPos,int,int), moveTo(Path,double), getPath/isDone/stop; Path.canReach/getNodeCount/getNodePos; ServerChunkCache.getChunkNow; native block collisions/fluid/floor checks. Search radius is bounded by remaining travel, actual route length is recomputed, all proposed nodes must be safe/loaded, proposals respect the owner's tighter repath interval. No route continuation can widen acceptance limits. Native SDK bytecode inspection and measured case evidence accompany the report.

Test-only DComeScene/DComeGameTests/DComeServer own a tagged isolated fixture. They remove vanilla free-will behaviors through the public native test API while leaving real AI/navigation/physics enabled. Test player setup may position the player; actor position is set only at spawn, before acceptance. The connected-client requester walks through the unchanged native client driver's ordinary input action after COME. None of these classes/descriptors enter the release JAR.

# D10 — Independent physical component qualification

**OWNED_GATES_PASS for D10.** Exact source `4c2c3d4a09d331181e8a8b7fd90386f3f63ca056`, tree `6d1b550a575d31da68dd3fb61f3414bd1bfcf350`, passed [consolidated run 41004294448](https://github.com/senavirathne/CognitiveCraft-public/actions/runs/41004294448), attempt 1. One qualification job and one production build ran every required D10 case and all affected D00–D09 regressions. The complete frozen verifier was rerun independently against downloaded raw evidence and reproduced both reports byte for byte. D11 is NOT_EXECUTED.

## Exact predecessor and scope

Continue qualified D09 at source `7e5bb6ad3205883342e3dfed9423607b306dcb1e`, tree `e535b197acddfdb75b95c8821357297ed341d7c0`, release SHA-256 `e7f4563413388c92c763d856600201e609130acf2f2eef01224f24f90965255e`, final docs `cb32d44a5cbb04a851803fcdc57bb23442a27933`. Its run was `40849502026`, attempt 1, artifact `12886823722`, ZIP SHA-256 `9a9bb5d01d8dd60928f47eb806d8e6d9187d983e8ccb0d0850fcff08939f8751`. The original qualified JSON SHA-256 is `414c8b1a83ec864f5867ffed7b640f5f51815ff2faf7b1e5eac75c91635d3f90`.

The frozen B source/docs bases remain unchanged. No peer/A/I00 code was imported. The cc.cd/1.0.0 contract is unchanged, byte-identical in source/docs, with manifest SHA-256 `e1e97de64c8c8934d51b47bba143a1fccb49e9fedb8882380fc5cdd3fe008cb3` and 57 canonical fixtures.

The complete original campaign is preserved from design commit `37fbf49e2aec4eddb3c7600217e585a1b349e48f`; its campaign Git blob is `560109a7183b9e4091abc34a43b6e8bb6b0a6a06`. The [frozen execution plan](D10-frozen-plan.json) retains all 48 IDs/expectations and fixes each origin, item, quantity, case variation seed, expected disposition and limits before the first qualification candidate. There are 12 storage, 12 mobility/follow, 12 courier and 12 handoff cases. The continuous D10 world has seed 20261027 and test-world tag `d1000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001`; every case requires two actual native clients. Host GameTests use their separately recorded actual native seed 0 and claim zero connected clients.

## Changes and boundaries

The [API and observer boundary](D10_API.md) describes request generation, actual native observations, independent assertions, two real clients, and saved-region observation. Two owned adapter corrections are included: exact vanilla incarnation eligibility; bounded follow navigation that validates the unwalked suffix of a potentially reused native path and reports insufficient travel allowance as TRAVEL_LIMIT. Production descriptors/entrypoints remain frozen; these adapters are inert until J02.

Native restart evidence deliberately distinguishes live vectors from native disk vectors. The courier is cut after pickup: live/saved/restored 6/7/2. The handoff is live 5/5 while the test-only fault withholds the actual recipient entity-chunk write; saved/restored 5/1 remains UNKNOWN. Original entity/marker/slot bytes are observed, never rewritten to manufacture recovery. New processes cannot inherit in-memory sessions/cargo. A 100-native-tick read-only window checks absence of automatic replay. Marker reload requires unchanged incarnation/topology and a fresh lifecycle epoch. Native chunk tracking is witnessed during preparation; a fixed number of fast GameTest ticks does not prove asynchronous entity-chunk readiness.

The independent oracle derives full inventory distributions and classified external changes from native slots, identities and item entities; checks old stock, guard revalidation, no actor teleport/forced loads, original time/travel/scan/repath limits, save bytes, exact release/runtime identities, real client packets/menus and native PNG bytes. Unavailable inventories are never empty. Dead/unloaded/replaced native objects are explicitly labelled last-known/unavailable; their object snapshots are not current participant custody. An unloaded-route case witnesses an actually unloaded intermediate chunk before/after refusal; the bounded native refusal does not claim a whole-world reachability proof.

## Frozen consolidated acceptance

| Tier | Planned on the final exact candidate | Counter scope |
|---|---:|---|
| Owned Java | 264 | All 259 D00–D09 cases plus five DAdversarialBoundaryTest methods |
| Python | 106 | All 100 predecessor cases, exact D09 lock control, five D10-P01 corrupt-evidence controls |
| Distinct native host cases | 10 | Nine prior cases plus D10-GT01; 15 JVM phases, 12 owned XML observations and one unchanged baseline |
| Real-client cases | 53 | Five predecessor campaigns plus 48 distinct D10 cases under D10-CL01 |
| D10 component dispositions | 48 | Expected 21 PASS and 27 REFUSED_EXPECTED; refusal is a safety outcome, not fulfillment |
| New native screenshots | 24 | Cases 01/05/12 in each family, both real clients; 12 predecessor images also repeated |

D10-U01 preserves lineage for every typed refusal without granting effects. D10-P01 rejects swapped recipient, hidden residual, fabricated save flag, duplicated diagnostic effect label and wrong JAR. D10-CL01 accepts every frozen mandatory case only after actual native/client evidence. D10-GT01 witnesses actual native saves/reloads and UNKNOWN partial persistence. Pure/model consistency checks, host tests, client cases and observer samples are counted separately.

The existing owner workflow has one 90-minute qualification job, one production build/JAR, and sequential existing SDK/Docker, module, Python, native, client and independent-oracle steps. All core/providers/fabric tests and every affected D00–D09 native/client/ACL/resolution/metadata/performance gate repeat on that same candidate. Raw artifacts upload on failure. The explicit standing user instruction authorizes this consolidated D10 run through the established blocking-request mechanism; no D11 work is started.

Local implementation diagnostics are unqualified: 264 owned Java tests and 106 Python checks passed; the cumulative native diagnostic accepted 10 cases across 15 JVMs. Mock-driven fixture diagnostics do not establish connected-client qualification. These observations are not relabelled as final-candidate evidence. These local diagnostics carry zero final-candidate credit. The exact consolidated candidate and independent raw verification below supply qualification.

## Commands and next gate

Use the unchanged established build plan through `e2e/parallel_d/build.py`, the existing `e2e/runtime.py prepare/compile`, six sequential `client_runner.py` schedules D05–D10, `stage.py run --stage D10 --built`, `verify.py --stage D10`, and final ownership/docs checks. The case registry fixes exact method/case IDs and denominators. The existing frozen CI trigger patch remains unchanged.

J02 retains production authority/runtime activation; J05 retains original-owner custody, coordinated participant saves and settlement. D11 is the next prompt and is NOT_EXECUTED. Stop after D10.

## Consolidated attempt history

The [attempt history](evidence/d10/attempt-history.json) retains all failed original ZIPs as hashed parts, original job logs and independent raw reviews. [restore-attempt.py](evidence/d10/restore-attempt.py) reconstructs each original ZIP and checks every part, the complete digest, size, member count and CRC. Every restore helper was exercised on fresh output. Each failed candidate receives zero final qualification credit.

Candidate 1 (`0f6d576bf214d80a9d16ce9ba4b0488484e8ecd2`, run `40903330196`) stopped because the actual server selection ray selected another block. Observer position/view preparation was synchronized before the same selection guard. Candidate 2 (`5bd5d4efb173dacdd210121303e903a88a646177`, run `40912642058`) completed the first native storage terminal but client collection read an empty live console acknowledgment during its write. D10 now retries only incomplete live console acknowledgments within the unchanged deadline and still requires the same nonce; final evidence parsing remains strict.

Independent review of the first two candidates rehashed all 681/683 manifested raw files, inspected the actual release/fixture separation, reconciled 2,571 module cases including 264 owned Java cases, accepted all 106 Python cases and 10 host cases, and reverified all five predecessor client campaigns in each failed artifact. These partial measurements cannot substitute for the missing complete 48-case D10 client campaign. Original ZIP membership and manifest hashes separately identified two local extraction nonmembers; they were preserved outside authentic raw evidence with hashes recorded in the attempt history.

Candidate 3 (`b39e77eaa24660e6844d5ea812825ce591fc8eb5`, run `40990898024`) preserved complete collection for storage cases 01–04, then attempted to fill unloaded chunks before positioning the observers for case 05. The native console reported the unloaded position; the real client subsequently stood on ground Y-60 rather than the requested Y201. The new fixture waits for normal player-loaded chunks, records each actual native stone block and zero forced chunks, and only then positions observers and admits the next case. The distant observer preparation uses the same guarded sequence. The independent oracle reconciles all 49 preparation records with native stdout and their admission clocks. No case expectation or bound changed. Candidate 3 retains zero final qualification credit; all 705 manifested raw files, 2,571 module cases, 106 Python checks, 10 host cases, five predecessor client campaigns and four native component terminals were independently checked.

Candidate 4 (`91ff66f1afe17585288bf922a21498590f635a7a`, run `40994010946`) completed client collection through storage/mobility cases01–12 and produced native courier01 vector9/3/3. The inventory observer then copied the villager chest-top height201.875 onto bare floor; its unchanged position witness correctly timed out after the observer fell to201. Independent review of all874 manifested raw files found a second mandatory failure in mobility11: the original1200-tick expiry and38 paused ticks were correct, but the reduced travel control ended UNREACHABLE rather than the frozen required TRAVEL_LIMIT. A cached native path had one valid unwalked waypoint, which the adapter incorrectly refused.

The correction places observers on the witnessed platform and allows a nonempty native path suffix while preserving the original guards and assertion. The [before/after local native diagnostic](evidence/d10/local-follow-diagnostic.json) reproduces old-adapter rejection and accepts the same assertion after correction; explicit mock targets provide zero client/qualification credit. Candidate4 also retains zero final qualification credit. Its raw review accepts24 component native outcomes and explicitly records the mobility11 oracle failure; these are partial observations, not a completed48-case campaign.

Candidate 5 (`594ab14677c87c6453fc95f3b80b52b4b456cbc7`, run `40998463178`) completed all 48 client schedules and both real native restart cuts. Its original artifact contains 1,112 manifested raw files, independently rehashed. All 2,571 module cases, 264 owned Java cases, 106 Python checks and 10 host cases passed. The unchanged D08 oracle rejected SUCCESS WITHDRAW at tick 508: **56.148533 ms**, above the frozen **50 ms p99** limit (250 ms maximum). The sample remains recorded as failure, without exclusion or a proven root-cause claim. Independent D10 review accepted 47 cases and rejected COURIER-08: its inventories and dropped-item UUID/type/count were unchanged, but natural drop motion crossed ticks 19765–19766. It receives zero final qualification credit.

Candidate 6 captures immediate same-tick native images before each courier primitive and retains exact inventory/drop equality after refusals. Rival and competing primitive timers measure their own calls. The [12-case local courier diagnostic](evidence/d10/local-atomic-courier-diagnostic.json) accepts the strengthened checks with explicit mock players and zero client/qualification credit. The entire D00–D09 regression schedule, all 48 D10 scenarios, every original timing/travel/scan/deadline bound and both D08 performance limits remain unchanged for the new consolidated run.

# D00 — frozen contract and isolated tooling

**OWNED_GATES_PASS for D00.** Source `313f32b80f6b4c1c6e8182982f40c85d417d38ba` passed [qualification run 40645634832, attempt 2](https://github.com/senavirathne/CognitiveCraft-public/actions/runs/40645634832/attempts/2). D01 is the next prompt and has not been started. D11 branch readiness and production registration remain deferred.

## Implemented behavior

The D-owned pure Java namespace provides immutable cc.cd/1.0.0 projections and a strict canonical UTF-8/integer-only codec. Unknown versions/fields, malformed bytes, duplicate keys, non-NFC strings, unsafe numbers, invalid topology/permissions, mismatched assistance roots and unsupported custody claims fail closed. Contextual observations are separate in-process inputs. A decoded ALLOW or proof reference grants no world authority, Job/effect ownership or settlement.

Owned tooling freezes stage case IDs and seeds; collects raw JUnit/Python XML and artifact identities; independently verifies outcomes; audits protected blobs/modes and core bytecode; and supplies an isolated Docker network, server/client directories and a standalone fixture mod. The D fixture compiles against the established Loom gameTest classpath using an owner-local Gradle init script. Its descriptor registers only D tests, and its tagged-world test authority is absent from the actual release JAR. The existing build files, production descriptors and global harness APIs are unchanged. Only the ten exact frozen baseline workflow trigger edits are permitted.

[Implemented API and limits](API.md) · [Frozen contract](contracts/README.md) · [Decisions](decisions.md).

Expected rejection/refusal validates the transport safeguard; it is not gameplay fulfillment. The two remaining Java checks cover malformed/unknown input and deep immutability. The 26 Docker checks cover actual native/release packaging, forbidden source/mode changes, shared volumes/networks, unknown stages, native imports/constant-pool descriptors and missing/duplicate/tampered evidence.

## Execution and corrections

The user's 28 October instruction authorizes early source Actions and Docker for the observed Java 25/SDK/Docker blockers. One 90-minute qualification job reuses the established Minecraft 26.3 / Java 25 / Loader 0.19.5 / Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3 / Loom 1.18.1 stack, checksum-verified SDK cache, original E2E Dockerfile and existing client/server drivers. The Docker tools image adds Git only. Its exact image IDs and pinned base digest are in the qualification record.

Three source workflow runs, five total attempts, were required. The earlier failures remain in [attempt history](evidence/attempt-history.json): a BuildKit base-tag inspection failure; transient exact-version Maven not-found responses; ambiguous inherited parameterized display IDs; and a timed-out Mercury download. The fixes explicitly load the same pinned Docker image and add method names through the D-owned JUnit configuration. Repository failures were retried on unchanged candidates after the exact official URLs became available. No version migration, baseline test-body edit, reduced scenario, relaxed threshold or fabricated native proof was used. Successful retries do not erase the original evidence.

The executable command plan remains in source `e2e/parallel_d/README.md` and `.github/workflows/parallel-d-qualification.yml`. One successful production build supplies all phases; stage collection consumes it with `--built`. The independent oracle validates actual XML/outcomes, hashes, ownership and frozen StageManifest semantics. Raw results live in this separate docs repo and Actions artifacts, preserving the measured source SHA.

## Boundaries and next gate

D00 adds no metadata persistence, storage resolver, physical transfer, navigation or conversation runtime. Its native fixture is compiled and packaging-qualified; no physical GameTest or real client was run. PlayerD_A and PlayerD_B are distinct configured identities, with no observed-client credit. Integrated root/owner/effect/save fields remain null and J-blocked. No live-model gate or save-qualified settlement is claimed.

Changed source groups are the owned storage contract/test namespace, `e2e/parallel_d/**`, the new owner workflow and ten exact trigger-only patches. Docs changes are limited to `docs/implementation/parallel-d/**`; the real shared index and global manifest remain unchanged. No docs Actions, production activation or merges are included.

**Next: D01 — Storage registry metadata and bounded persistence.** D00's owned gates permit that stage; this handoff stops here. J01/J02 own production registration and authority adapters. C08/D11 and qualified A10/I00 remain prerequisites for later joint integration, not evidence established by this D00 pass.

# D04 resolution API and trusted observation boundary

StorageResolver and StorageResolution live in core/kernel/storage; RecipientResolver lives in core/kernel/logistics. All are inert pure Java. Constructors require every port and an authenticated server tick supplier. No Minecraft/Fabric dependency, automatic production registration, IO worker, tick task, discovery index, movement or inventory mutation is added.

`StorageResolver.begin(scope, StorageSelector, operation)` accepts only a strict decoded frozen StorageSelector and INSPECT/DEPOSIT/WITHDRAW. The selector is untrusted data. `Query.step()` advances at most 16 metadata records once per increasing server tick; a second call during the same tick returns the same state. PENDING has no endpoint. Truncation at 256 inspected records or discovery of a 129th permission-filtered candidate returns UNKNOWN. Full scans choose only eligible observed candidates, with exact named ambiguity checked across visible matches. A missing citizen default returns CLARIFY even if an arbitrary nearby chest exists. Type filtering supports only chest single/double and barrel.

`NativePort.view(scope,tick)` must return a fresh authenticated View with lifecycle epoch, monotonic complete query revision and server caller/controlled-actor positions. Its revision must cover all registered-candidate load/topology/capacity/protection, caller visibility, organization membership and citizen control changes that could alter the answer, including previously denied candidates. If this complete observation cannot be supplied, complete must be false and the query returns UNKNOWN. J01 is responsible for the actual projection from existing owners. Query methods must run on the server actor; no port may force chunk loads or execute inventory effects. Anchor positions are captured only from this port, never decoded player coordinates. Later position movement does not rerank the captured query.

`NativePort.observe` must return exact scope/binding/generation/lifecycle/tick, supported/loaded flags and operation-specific capacity eligibility from the native adapter. Every binding member is within radius 16 horizontal and +/-4 vertical relative to the captured anchor. Canonical first-member block-center squared milliblock distance orders candidates, followed by x/y/z and canonical UUID. Distance bounds are tested before multiplication. UNKNOWN/ineligible capacity, unsupported or unloaded native state cannot win. Stored acknowledged binding identity must match the fresh native topology/incarnation/generation and epoch. The final winner is observed and authorized again; a changed final answer returns UNKNOWN without reranking a fallback.

`SelectionPort.consume` retrieves and consumes only an actual server-retained selection for authenticated scope/selection UUID. Its returned Selection contains a strict frozen SelectionWitness plus the registered storage identity. The resolver checks the exact requested selection ID, scope/world/domain/principal, dimension/lifecycle, capture/expiry, registered member coordinates/type and fresh native binding. `SelectionPort.current` must independently verify that retained caller/actor identity, current reach/line-of-sight/protection and native block-entity live-instance token still match the actual server object/topology. Decoding or constructing witness data does not install this port or create a retained capability. Unregistered selected chests cannot be discovered or marked by D04. Witnesses expire within the frozen maximum 40 ticks and do not survive restart.

StorageResolution has fieldless PENDING/CLARIFY/UNAVAILABLE/UNKNOWN/UNSUPPORTED dispositions, or a server-created opaque Bound endpoint. Refusal results carry no private UUID, label, count, stock, ACL or hidden reason. `Query.work()` is a server-only diagnostic (inspected records, candidate counter and tick), never a client projection. The overflow counter may report 129 only to prove the refusal; no 129th native candidate is observed or ranked.

`Bound.current(scope)` re-observes complete view, snapshot, accepted citizen control (for roles), D03 Decision and native identity/capacity/selection. It rechecks the view/snapshot after observations. The accepted decision expires after two ticks and must be resolved again; a wire ALLOW cannot mint a Bound. `Bound.wire()` supplies the strict frozen STORAGE ResolvedEndpoint only while current. It remains a projection. J02 must use the same current observations and effect critical section; the endpoint is not an A capability, lease, save witness or settlement.

`RecipientResolver.Port.view` is an immutable complete bounded list (maximum 256), scoped to the authenticated caller and current tick. Its monotonic revision covers name, visibility/control/load/identity/policy changes; epoch fences restart. `lookup` returns a fresh immutable Citizen projection for the exact requested stable citizen ID. A Citizen includes scope, epoch, citizen/entity UUID, generation/policy revision, display name, dimension, inventory revision digest, tick, visible/controlled/loaded and explicit permitted operations. These are server observations, never accepted from client endpoint claims. A role beneficiary requires current control; a visible permitted recipient can remain usable without granting caller control or inventory inspection. The query scans at most 16 rows per tick and 128 visible eligible citizens; direct addressed/explicit-ID lookup still enforces scope/epoch/visibility/control/permission/load. Missing/private/unloaded/foreign gives uniform UNAVAILABLE. Display labels match by the same frozen NFC/Unicode fold, with no fuzzy selection.

A recipient Bound privately retains the accepted citizen/entity/generation/epoch/policy identity. `fresh(scope)` looks up that stable ID, revalidates all live permissions/control/load and returns an immutable current projection; it never searches the old name. Renames alone preserve the bound recipient, while entity replacement, generation change, policy revocation, unload or caller swap fail closed. J04 projects this current identity into the frozen CITIZEN seam before requesting A/B work. No new citizen registry, POI registry or second persistence owner is introduced.

Test-only StorageResolutionTestSupport and StorageResolutionProbe are explicitly rejected from production packaging. Probe data and timings are pure port observations with null integrated roots/save proof. Existing D02 physical fixtures are unchanged and repeated separately; their native evidence does not upgrade D04's synthetic projections to production/client proof.

# D02 API and native hook boundary

`StorageBindingRules` in core has immutable Member, Topology and Binding values. It canonicalizes members by (x,y,z,incarnation UUID), rejects unsupported shapes, duplicate members, nonadjacent/vertical double chests and incorrect facing axes, and hashes the frozen canonical topology JSON including its final LF. Wire encoding/decoding passes through D's unchanged cc.cd/1.0.0 codec. Endpoint identity also includes a live lifecycle epoch. These values carry no authorization or save tier.

`StorageRegistry.prepareBinding` checks caller/world, optimistic global and record revisions, fresh supplied BIND policy and the next binding generation. It writes UNKNOWN intent through the same bounded metadata owner before native writes. First binding remains PENDING_BIND; rebinding advances generation/revision and becomes UNVERIFIED. `acknowledgeBinding` requires that exact intent, an actual matching live observation and supplied COMMIT_BIND policy, rechecked before IO. It records ACTIVE metadata after acknowledgement. The authority provider must attest native observations; wire input is never its authority. Loss or denial between steps leaves a non-live pending history. This is not an inventory/effect journal or cross-owner save settlement.

`StorageIncarnationAdapter` requires a ServerLevel, stable world UUID and explicit supplied policy; construction/install and every native operation require the server thread. One owner is allowed per level. `updateMetadata` installs an acknowledged immutable snapshot and builds bounded position/marker indexes outside any scheduled tick. `plan` captures exact loaded block-entity instances and lifecycle versions, creates prospective UUIDs only on the server, and writes no markers. `write` requires the durable exact intent and unchanged instances/topology/lifecycle, rechecks provided native authority, uses a private one-use marker permit, then returns a live observation. No catch-all Container support exists.

`resolve` requires ACTIVE acknowledged metadata and fresh loaded native state. Double chests must have actual complementary LEFT/RIGHT states, equal facing and mutual native connected positions. OPEN/lid changes and labels preserve identity. Replacement retires the old marker in the live owner; marker changes, removal and topology mutations invalidate captured endpoints. A verified reload can issue a fresh lifecycle epoch after complete matching checks; it cannot revive a captured endpoint. Duplicates remain quarantined until operator resolution, with bounded overflow closing the adapter. No API grants permissions, changes inventory, forces chunks, schedules ticks, takes retention, or constructs Jobs authority. Installation, shutdown and operator resolution belong to J01.

## Verified Minecraft 26.3 methods

Discovery used the checksum-locked native server JAR prepared by existing `scripts/headless.py`; the qualification artifact repeats `javap -p -c` against its actual installed bytes. Chest and barrel call through their superclass chain to these exact base methods. No mappings or versions are changed.

| Owner | Verified descriptor | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| BlockEntity | `loadAdditional(ValueInput): void` | Read namespaced versioned incarnation UUID/generation; malformed recognized markers refuse use. |
| BlockEntity | `saveAdditional(ValueOutput): void` | Persist identity only; no ACL, contents, role or save claim. |
| BlockEntity | `preRemoveSideEffects(BlockPos, BlockState): void` | Actual LevelChunk replacement path retires the old incarnation. |
| BlockEntity | `setRemoved(): void` | Invalidate live endpoints before removal/unload. |
| BlockEntity | `setBlockState(BlockState): void` | Invalidate on type/facing/chest topology changes; ignore opening. |
| BlockEntity | `setLevel(Level): void`, `clearRemoved(): void` | Observe loaded markers and candidate reload integrity. |

The mixin class is release code under D's allowed `fabric/storage/mixin` prefix but remains unregistered in the production mixin descriptor. Only `parallel-d.mixins.json` in the separate fixture mod registers it. Test authority, benchmark and native evidence classes are absent from the production JAR. The performance baseline fixture explicitly disables these mixins and runs the exact qualified D01 JAR.

Only tagged fixture worlds are used during independent D02 qualification. Production lifecycle/startup ordering must install the J01 owner before observing eligible marker loads; no independent D code registers itself. Runtime duplicate and retirement indexes are not a new durable settlement owner. J05 must qualify interrupted native/metadata histories with A before integrated use.

# D03 — Storage ACLs, ownership and lifecycle policy

Status: **OWNED_GATES_PASS**. [Actions run 40677975122, attempt 1](https://github.com/senavirathne/CognitiveCraft-public/actions/runs/40677975122) completed successfully on the first candidate. Independent BRANCH_READY remains a D11 gate; production integration remains with J.

Qualified D02 predecessor: source `ffcd3f5f3d37fc0d590dacca0a88471bb7e5eee9`, tree `a51dc4711641afe9e85139cbfe756a282ff3e132`, JAR SHA-256 `ff505ffabd76d61f46aeb0569b0afeb6274aa1443a4276d554208129593e1ed1`, final docs `b4294e84e602b929d61dcc9c4b03c9e224b71182`, run 40672315339 attempt 1. Its raw qualified result SHA-256 is `793a14cb1444a4b44c43a4b1766542e52779023c9ff22450140c385d6f255bde`. Frozen B source/docs ancestry remains unchanged. No peer C/A implementation is read or imported.

The exact design input remains `37fbf49e2aec4eddb3c7600217e585a1b349e48f`, prompt D03. The cc.cd/1.0.0 contract manifest/schema and all 57 fixtures remain byte-identical in source and docs.

D03 separates owner identity, explicit operation grants, trusted organization/citizen control and native vetoes. Empty ACL or missing registration grants no mod-actor operation, including for an owner. An explicit deposit share permits selecting its endpoint but cannot inspect or withdraw private stock. Player, citizen, organization and explicitly public ownership never imply public access. Visibility omits private labels/UUIDs/totals and gives the identical fieldless unavailable result for absent and private targets. This policy does not change vanilla access.

Metadata administration has a separate supplied current-control and delegation policy so an empty private record can be administered. Grant/revoke permissions are separate; grants require a bounded explicit ceiling. Ownership transfer requires old-owner control plus explicit target policy, clears all ACL grants, advances record/ACL/generation revisions, clears bindings and leaves stale role references. No previous owner grant silently survives. See [D03_API.md](D03_API.md).

The frozen candidate plan contains 133 cumulative owned Java tests (33 new), 56 Python checks (six new), and the four prior D02 native cases repeated on this candidate. D03 adds zero native/client cases. D03-P01 runs one actual Java probe with a persistent metadata owner and 100 consecutive seeded transitions, then compares its actual decisions and persisted metadata with an independent Python model. The transition observations support one Python campaign case; they are not 100 additional test passes. Grant/revoke/transfer/membership each occur 25 times, with seed 20261027 plus the case ordinal. Every step checks old-decision rejection and a fresh-decision positive/negative control. This is pure policy/metadata evidence, not physical authority or an A save claim.

The frozen sequence input is `e2e/parallel_d/campaigns/D03-acl-100.json`, SHA-256 `05b44f59c7e4cd1b55b32562a81d6c3747dfa89021c2fda5a5096293a89ab3e5`. Case IDs, expected model, bounds and registry are frozen before the first candidate request. No test expectation or old threshold is weakened. The existing D01 metadata fixtures now explicitly supply only the INSPECT/DEPOSIT delegation needed by their unchanged assertions; new authority defaults deny grants/transfer.

A decision expires within two ticks and still re-observes current identity, ACL, organization/control revision and native policy at each effect check. Each evaluation scans at most 32 ACL rows, batches at most 33 organization IDs once, and makes bounded control/native queries. Enumeration is capped by the existing 4096-record snapshot ceiling. There is no cache, scheduled tick task, retention owner, inventory/effect ledger or new production entrypoint. The cumulative native lifecycle benchmark repeats the exact unchanged D01 control schedule; new pure ACL evaluation p50/p95/p99/max observations are recorded separately, without claiming a baseline ratio for a policy absent from D02.

Local diagnostics precede source freeze and have no qualified source/JAR counts. The user authorized Actions and Docker for blocking dependencies/tests; the existing single D job builds one candidate release, repeats all module/owned cases, uses the established integrity-checked SDK/Docker environment and emits partial artifacts on failure. This following report commit retains the exact measured results below while source stays frozen.

J01 must translate the existing OrganizationRegistry/citizen/native projections on the server side, install lifecycle/selection fences, supply current target acceptance/delegation, and publish immutable revocation observations for the metadata IO worker. D03 imports none of those owners and does not call native APIs from that worker. J02 owns critical-section effect-time authority. J05 must exercise revocation during real physical travel and coordinated interrupted saves. D04 is next and remains unstarted by D03.

# D09 API / current authority and live atomicity boundary

RecipientDeliveryPolicy.Goal(request,carrier,recipient,source,sourceCitizen,storageSource,item,quantity) binds stable identities and source kind. Target excludes labels/positions and validates current authorized CitizenProjection. Session tracks READY/IN_FLIGHT/DELIVERED_LIVE/BLOCKED/UNCERTAIN and at most8 batches. acceptExisting admits explicit existing cargo without mutation. observe accepts only exact conserving native deltas. A refusal retains in-flight units and is terminal; uncertainty creates no completion or replay authority.

VillagerTransferAdapter(ServerLevel,Villager,Actor,Scope,MinecraftStorageAdapter,Authority) registers nothing. Authority.observe returns current exact Actor, controlled/exclusiveSender/exclusiveRecipient, existingSourceAuthorized, protectionAllowed, custodyRevision and native interactionLimit. These are trusted server observations under A ownership, never decoded client assertions. SourceSelection binds authenticated principal/request/sender, current native slot objects and explicit quantities. existing(session,boundRecipient,exactItem,selection) yields an opaque Cargo after validating current source custody and all native images. withdraw additionally requires a current authorized source binding and free carrier slot. It never takes a player or third villager inventory.

handoff(Cargo) is one-shot even on refusal. It revalidates the same bound recipient/native instance, current projection/control, exact native classes, full8-slot images, attributed cargo, storage ACL if relevant, capacity, current native separation≤min(2.5,interactionLimit), line of sight and protection. All allocated replacements precede final callbacks/preimage verification. Its exact fixed native backing lists support the non-yielding16-index write section. Unsupported class profiles refuse before mutation. No dropped-item transfer, compensation, duplicate delivery or automatic retry is provided.

MinecraftNavigationAdapter.recipient(actor,scope,boundRecipient) captures one current native recipient position. Every externally owned tick revalidates the same native instance/lifecycle/DEPOSIT grant and stops its own route on target motion beyond.25 blocks. It retains D06 finite limits and last accepted observation semantics at a guard stop. Actual current tick/feet and native navigation_done remain separate raw observations.

J02 must register the capability, provide original-root actor/participant resources and current inventory-writer fences, charge actual elapsed/travel under the original remaining allowance, and verify installed runtime transformations preserve the primitive. D09's exact SDK class lock is a measured local primitive profile, not a general promise about arbitrary containers/mod sets. Native stack-object identity is ephemeral provenance; System.identityHashCode in private fixture evidence is diagnostic only and is never an authority/save ID.

J05 must qualify both native participant saves, custody after cancellation, crash/restart ambiguity and any separately authorized continuation. Death/unload fixtures establish actual live unavailability; setRemoved(UNLOADED_TO_CHUNK) does not assert a completed entity participant save. Native menus after removal may retain the last referenced inventory object and are explicitly unavailable observations. LIVE_DEPOSITED/DELIVERED_LIVE never imply JOURNAL_ACKNOWLEDGED, PARTICIPANT_SAVES_CONFIRMED or ORIGINAL_OWNER_SETTLED. Production hooks, registration, A journal/effect ownership, automatic replay and shared documentation integration remain deferred.

# D05 storage architecture and support matrix

The pure core owns eligibility and immutable observations. The current-loader adapter owns finite native reads behind current D03 authorization and the existing D02 incarnation owner. J01 owns installation/projections; A/J02 own effects and original-root/custody/save settlement. The adapter remains inert until explicitly supplied by that owner. Native test authority and client/server fixtures live only in the D harness. No production entrypoint, second registry, discovery scheduler, effect ledger or inventory ledger is installed.

| Native container | Independent D support | Required bounds / refusal | Evidence scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vanilla normal single chest | MVP implemented; activation deferred J01 | 27 loaded slots; current marker/policy; no lock/loot/obstruction | D05-GT01 and D05-CL01 required |
| Vanilla normal double chest | MVP implemented; activation deferred J01 | Two matching loaded members; 54 unique slots; both policies/locks/loot/lids checked | D02 topology plus D05-GT01/CL01 required |
| Vanilla barrel | MVP implemented; activation deferred J01 | 27 loaded slots; current marker/policy; no lock/loot | D05-GT01 and D05-CL01 required |
| Trapped chest | Disabled / explicitly unsupported | Exact block/class guard rejects ChestBlockEntity inheritance | Native trapped refusal control required; no positive support |
| Ender chest | Disabled / unsupported | Player-linked semantics are outside MVP | Pending its own adapter/native tests |
| Shulker box, all colors | Disabled / unsupported | Movable/nested storage is outside MVP | Pending its own adapter/native tests |
| Hopper | Disabled / unsupported | Automation/sided rules are outside MVP | Pending its own adapter/native tests |
| Furnace, blast furnace, smoker | Disabled / unsupported | Processing/sided slot rules are outside MVP | Pending their own adapters/native tests |
| Modded/custom storage | Disabled / unsupported | A Container cast or inherited class cannot grant support | Pending explicit registered adapter/native tests |
| Unregistered, incomplete or unloaded topology | No live eligibility | Unknown/unloaded is never empty; no chunk forcing | Typed native refusal; fieldless client unavailable |
| Any locked/unresolved-loot container | Refused | Check flags before every slot read; do not unpack loot | Actual native lock/loot refusal controls |
| Unsupported/non-default/nested item stacks | Refused | Native identity/fingerprint and exact slot limits required | Pure guards and native modified/container item controls |

The matrix describes implementation scope, not a qualification result. Read the current [D05 report](D05.md) and [stage manifest](stage-manifest.json) for measured status. Non-MVP rows remain disabled even after the supported rows qualify. Shared architecture indexes remain owned by J06; this owned page does not modify their historical statuses.

The client observer is separate from vanilla container synchronization. Native menus demonstrate actual contents and ordinary network synchronization. Permission-filtered mod observations independently require INSPECT, with identical unavailable output for private/absent/deposit-only access. A test observer cannot grant native access, synthesize receipts or confirm participant saves.

# D04 — Deterministic storage and recipient resolution

Status: **OWNED_GATES_PASS**. [Actions run 40712423016, attempt 1](https://github.com/senavirathne/CognitiveCraft-public/actions/runs/40712423016) completed successfully. D11 retains independent BRANCH_READY; J retains production integration and release qualification.

Source/docs remain descendants of the frozen B bases. No peer implementation is read or imported.

The exact design input remains `37fbf49e2aec4eddb3c7600217e585a1b349e48f`, prompt D04. The cc.cd/1.0.0 manifest/schema and 57 fixtures remain unchanged and byte-identical in source/docs.

StorageResolver resolves registered permission-filtered metadata through required fresh loaded native observations. DEFAULT/OWNER_ROLE first bind a controlled visible citizen, then use that stable citizen's exact role assignment and generation. No missing role falls back to a random or nearest chest. NAMED uses exact NFC/Unicode casefold within visible scope; visible namesakes clarify, including when one cannot currently accept the requested operation. SELECTED consumes a server-retained witness, then rechecks its request ID, caller/world/domain, dimension, lifecycle, expiry, registered member and current server incarnation. NEAREST_PUBLIC requires an explicit PUBLIC grant for the requested operation. Deposit-only named shares remain usable without an INSPECT grant.

Each query inspects at most 256 metadata records, at most 16 per server tick, and detects a 129th permission-filtered candidate before a native observation. At most 128 candidates can be observed/ranked. Repeated calls in one tick do no further work. Caller or actor position is captured once. Every member must be loaded and within 16 blocks horizontally (circular radius) and +/-4 vertically from that captured anchor. Double chests rank by their canonical first member's block center; distance is squared milliblocks, then integer x/y/z, then canonical UUID string. Bounds checks precede squaring. Unknown capacity, unsupported adapter, unloaded identity and denied final operation cannot win. Incomplete/truncated/changed discovery returns UNKNOWN without a partial endpoint; final refusal never falls back to a farther candidate.

RecipientResolver uses required read-only citizen projections with stable citizen/entity/generation/lifecycle identity, visibility/control/permission and current server tick. Namesakes clarify. Unloaded, foreign, private and absent recipients have the same fieldless unavailable result. A bound delivery checks its accepted stable identity and current policy; rename alone cannot reroute it to another citizen who takes the old display name. Named MVP places use the same registered storage selector; other landmarks remain unsupported, with no new POI registry.

See [D04_API.md](D04_API.md) for the trusted port obligations, immutable results, work bounds and effect-time limits.

# D07 API / trusted owner boundary

FollowPolicy.start(UUID session, Actor identity, Point feet, Point authenticatedPlayer, long tick, long ownerDeadline, double remainingTravel) admits one finite session. Session.advance(Facts) yields immutable FollowState with STOP, WAIT, MOVE_PROPOSAL or EXPIRED; its session, original acceptance, shrinking deadline, cumulative travel/pause, observation/repath counters and actual feet remain observable. Session.stop(reason) is independent of a model/provider and terminality is permanent. Facts are trusted observations, never decoded client claims.

FollowObservationAdapter(ServerLevel,Mob,Authority) installs nothing. Authority returns current native Control(actor,authorized,reserved,deadline,remainingTravel) under the existing exclusive A movement owner. The optional trusted native player lookup supports owner-supplied observations; default lookup is the live server player list. start requires the same actual authenticated ServerPlayer. Route.step must run once per native tick; cancel stops its own path. No caller may tick it after surrendering actor ownership. Competing live navigation is refused without stopping the competitor's path. Initial and later native player dimension/liveness, actor UUID and control generations are revalidated.

J02 maps the original A root, actor custody and remaining budget/deadline into the injected authority and charges actual elapsed/displacement there. J05 owns durable cancellation/restart settlement. These components do not create an action root, A journal, inventory effect or save receipt. Native follow and rendered clients establish LIVE_OBSERVED behavior only. Production registration remains deferred.

# D03 policy API and privacy boundary

`StorageAccessPolicy` is pure Java under `core/kernel/storage`. It requires an immutable snapshot supplier, OrganizationMembershipPort, ControlPort, ProtectionPort and a current server tick supplier. No permissive constructor/default port or public Decision constructor exists. Scope consists of authenticated world/domain/principal plus optional controlled citizen actor; constructing or decoding a wire DTO never supplies those ports or native authority.

`evaluate(scope, storage, operation)` independently checks INSPECT, DEPOSIT, WITHDRAW, ASSIGN, RENAME, GRANT and REVOKE. Runtime operations require ACTIVE registered metadata, its acknowledged binding reference, an explicit matching ACL operation and a current matching native projection. PLAYER grants match principal; CITIZEN grants match the exact actor and fresh control projection; ORGANIZATION grants require current known member rights; PUBLIC grants contain only explicitly configured inspect/deposit/withdraw. A metadata owner does not implicitly receive operation permissions. Organization-owned records additionally obey the current organization policy, so unknown organization state denies access. Known outsider permissions can only come from an explicit trusted organization policy plus an explicit record grant.

`OrganizationMembershipPort.observe(scope, organizations)` is a single read-only IO-free batch of at most 33 organization IDs. Its scope and monotonic membership revision fence decisions; no organization display name is consulted. Missing membership is UNKNOWN. ControlPort returns scope/subject/revision/known/control/delegation facts. ProtectionPort returns exact scope/storage/operation/generation/tick and native policy revision. Stale, mismatched, missing or UNKNOWN native facts cannot allow; the native provider may veto every mod allow. J01 must supply those current projections from qualified existing owners, without importing their implementation into D.

`Decision.current` re-evaluates policy even inside its two-tick validity window and compares scope/actor, operation, world/domain/principal, global registry revision, record revision, binding generation, ACL revision, owner and dependency revisions. Restoring rights at a later revision does not revive an old decision. `authorizesEffect` additionally requires ALLOW. These methods observe a point in time; J02 must call them in the same non-yielding authorized server critical section as an actual effect. They are not leases or A capabilities.

`Decision.wire` projects the unchanged cc.cd/1.0.0 StorageAccessDecision for server-side seams. A decoded ALLOW cannot construct the opaque in-process decision. Refusal projections may contain server-side requested identity/revisions and must not be sent directly to clients. StorageVisibility is the presentation boundary.

`StorageVisibility.lookup` returns either Visible(storage UUID, label, adapter, generation) or the same fieldless Unavailable singleton for missing/private/unknown/stale targets. `enumerate` and `named` return immutable visible entries only, sorted by stable identity. Matching uses the D01 Unicode/NFC casefold and never adds hidden matches or totals. No stock, ACL, owner data, filtered counts or private reason is exposed. Deposit-only callers can select an explicitly shared endpoint without gaining an INSPECT decision. Snapshot changes during discovery refuse publication of mixed results. This is a finite 4096-record scan, not a persistent discovery index or scheduled task.

`mayAdminister` separately checks current owner control and native administrative veto/delegation ceiling. PLAYER administration requires actual matching principal plus control; CITIZEN administration uses current citizen control; ORGANIZATION administration uses current trusted administrator/member policy; PUBLIC administration requires explicitly supplied operator control. This separate path permits administration of an empty private ACL without granting automation access. It does not install itself as StorageRegistry.Authority.

StorageRegistry adds `grant`, `revoke` and `transferOwnership`, preserving expected global/record revisions and its sole bounded asynchronous metadata IO owner. Authority.mayGrant and mayTransfer default to false. Initial ACL seeding, bulk replacement and individual grant require explicit delegation policy; current owner/control/action/ceiling is rechecked immediately before the pending write. Grant cannot widen beyond the provided operations. Revoke cannot imply grant. Duplicate ACL subjects are rejected rather than merged on load. A future malformed/ambiguous legacy snapshot remains read-only; no migration silently invents rights.

Transfer clears ACL and bindings, increments record/ACL/identity generations, sets UNVERIFIED, and retains older role references as stale. It never changes physical inventory or inherits the old owner's grant. A new owner needs a fresh explicit policy and binding. Registration/transfer target consent and native protection are J01 responsibilities behind the required supplied authority; text claiming ownership is never accepted by D. The metadata IO worker must read immutable current revocation projections, not call a game-thread native API. Existing registered data with unique ACL subjects retains the cc.storage-metadata/1 shape.

Test-only StorageAclSequenceProbe and StoragePolicyTestSupport supply synthetic projections in core test output and are explicitly prohibited from the release JAR. The probe creates actual metadata files and executes 100 transitions without resetting its history. The Python oracle independently checks canonical checksums, UUID/scope/operation/tick fences, every revision/generation/owner/ACL transition, old-decision refusal, fresh controls and final persisted state. Those observations have no native/client/root/save tier. The prior D02 standalone fixture is repeated unchanged as a physical regression and remains absent from production descriptors.

# D01 — storage registry metadata and bounded persistence

**OWNED_GATES_PASS for D01.** Exact source `ea1ff7ec9ab1fd16782c32130207aa7e5230442a` passed [Actions qualification 40662229204, attempt 1](https://github.com/senavirathne/CognitiveCraft-public/actions/runs/40662229204). The first candidate passed with one production build and no dependency retries. D02 is next and has not started; D11 branch readiness and production registration remain deferred.

## Resulting behavior

The D-owned pure Java registry stores metadata only. Registration produces PENDING_BIND until the future native binding adapter validates a target. Renames preserve world/storage UUID and generation. NFC display labels retain their spelling; pinned Unicode 16 full case folding affects lookup only. Namesakes remain ambiguous. Snapshot/record/assignment expected revisions prevent lost writes: two concurrent writes at one revision acknowledge exactly one.

Beneficiary defaults are a separate `(world, beneficiary, role)` table. Duplicate creation conflicts; reassignment requires the exact existing revision and explicit beneficiary/target authority. Shared or organization-owned storage can be a citizen's default without transferring ownership or adding ACL grants. Purpose roles do not act as defaults. Tombstones retain identities, advance generation and invalidate stale assignments, including after restart. Administrative policy is rechecked immediately before a write.

One bounded dedicated IO worker owns immutable snapshots and the world-directory file lock. It reserves replacement/rollback headroom, writes and forces a pending snapshot, stages and forces the previous copy, atomically replaces current, forces the directory, then acknowledges metadata. Queue overflow refuses without caller-thread IO. Missing, corrupt, unsupported, foreign-world, stale-pending and externally changed files preserve originals and open/read-fail safely. Only explicit fresh-directory initialization can create a new store. Disk-full refusal occurs before changing snapshot files; it does not evict identities or tombstones.

Hard limits are 4096 records/world including tombstones, 4096 beneficiary-role assignments, 32 ACL grants/record, four purpose roles and an 8 MiB serialized current snapshot. Versions, checksums, canonical bytes, complete ACLs, key uniqueness, worlds and referenced generations are strict. Inventory counts, Jobs, reservations, credits and effects are not part of the format. A metadata acknowledgement is not a Minecraft save acknowledgement.

# D08 API / custody and effect boundary

DeliveryPolicy.Goal carries one request/citizen, exact source/destination world/storage/dimension/participant identities, installed default-component Item and quantity1..64. admit returns explicit refusal; batch requires the entire proposed batch's capacity. Session.observe consumes native TransferObservation deltas and retains one original request across at most8 batches. LIVE_DEPOSITED/DELIVERED_LIVE are live observations and cannot satisfy an A completion receipt. Counts are bounded and conservation is explicit.

MinecraftTransferAdapter(ServerLevel,Villager,Actor,Scope,MinecraftStorageAdapter,Authority) registers nothing. Authority.observe must attest the current exact actor/control generation, exclusive custody and owner inventory revision while holding existing A resources in the supplied canonical stable-identity order. The fixture injects isolated authority only. J02 must verify the installed inventory/custody fence and all uncontrolled-writer behavior before production activation; unknown custody refuses. Native slot references, full carrier images and effect-boundary preimages add independent checks, including identical old stock. These are ephemeral batch provenance, not a replacement inventory/effect ledger.

withdraw(Session,sourceBinding,destinationBinding,exactNativeItem,Selection) returns a native delta plus an opaque private-constructor Batch. It uses a free carrier slot, never merges with existing stock and checks source/destination current identity/rights, full batch capacity and native reach before writing. A deliberate Selected witness carries the source/participant/slot, actual native stack object, admitted count, native observation tick and authenticated principal; it is validated again at the final boundary. No decoded UUID/ALLOW or client-coordinate selection grants authority. No API reads a ServerPlayer inventory.

deposit(Batch) is one-shot, even on refusal. It rejects foreign/missing/replayed tokens, changed custody revision/actor, altered carrier image/stack identity/components/count, stale endpoints/rights, capacity and reach. It removes only currently attributed units, then emits actual participant deltas; partial or exceptional changes remain UNCERTAIN and are never compensated or credited. Blockers preserve in-flight material at its actual/last-known custody location with a J reconciliation requirement. No return/deposit retry is automatically scheduled.

J02 allocates original-root step/effect identity before invoking the port, owns actor/storage locks, decrements original budgets and deadline, reconciles actual deltas and supplies native inventory mutation/custody fencing. J05 owns participant-save confirmation, ambiguous crash/restart/cancel settlement and any new continuation/return-custody authorization. The D08 native save/kill/reload case deliberately demonstrates different live vs saved participant images without providing those protocols. Public component observations cannot manufacture JOURNAL_ACKNOWLEDGED, PARTICIPANT_SAVES_CONFIRMED or ORIGINAL_OWNER_SETTLED evidence.

The storage port exposes currentEndpoint(Binding) only as a server-thread identity guard on an already admitted binding. It delegates to the existing incarnation owner, reads no slots, grants no permission and exports no stock. The courier checks this identity before operation authorization so a replaced endpoint reports STALE_ENDPOINT while an identity-preserving ACL revocation reports UNAUTHORIZED. Both guards repeat at the final non-yielding effect boundary.

# D10 API and observer boundary

## Production scope

No new domain API, scheduler, Job writer, effect ledger, retention owner or production initializer is added. StorageIncarnationAdapter.eligible now accepts only exact ChestBlockEntity/BarrelBlockEntity classes with their exact supported vanilla block states, matching the existing inventory adapters. Trapped/modded and other variants refuse before a marker write or inventory operation.

FollowObservationAdapter validates at most 32 unwalked native path nodes per proposal. Minecraft can return the current path object, whose prefix may already have been walked; the adapter creates a bounded nonempty suffix instead of truncating that live shared object (a single remaining native waypoint is valid), and records the actual native navigation path it owns. Remaining distance, original deadline and accumulated pauses remain monotonic; a remaining allowance unable to admit another native segment produces TRAVEL_LIMIT. The existing 8-block lookahead, 10-tick minimum repath interval, 1200-tick/128-block maximum and 100-tick pause are unchanged. Normal native no-path failures remain typed refusals. J02 must supply actual original runtime ownership/custody and cumulative allowances.

## Test-only request generation

DComponentCampaignServer selects only the frozen 48 cases in order, in one isolated continuous world, with fresh native actor/citizen/storage identities and two actual connected players. P1 owns normal requests; P2 performs the deposit-only positive case and specified interference. Before admission, actual observers load the normal region chunks from the existing flat-world ground; the fixture records every elevated stone floor block, loaded chunk and unchanged forced-chunk count before moving the observers to Y201. This also prepares the distant observer platform without loading the unknown intermediate route. Native storage selection uses the real server raycast before marker registration. Native menus display actual containers; eight villager slots have one empty display cell which is never counted as stock. No player inventory is inspected.

DComponentCase and its storage/mobility/courier/handoff subclasses generate requests and record native observations; they do not decide qualification. Component request/observation labels are diagnostic lineage, never A root/effect identity. Native inventories, block markers/NBT, entity identity/generation/visibility, native feet/path/counters, forced-chunk counts, clocks and measured adapter timings are recorded. Frames are emitted to stdout and committed as complete raw files at operation/terminal boundaries; the independent oracle requires exact agreement. The source release JAR cannot contain these classes or their authority.

DComponentCampaign is a collector over the unchanged native client driver/renderer/SDK. It captures both actual players, native entity/menu packets and screenshots. The storage privacy case permits only fieldless P2 feedback while P1 provides privileged native observation. Actual disconnect/dimension/STOP/interference conditions are observed at the server. Host fixture diagnostics use explicitly identified mocks and receive zero client credit.

## Save/restart observation

save_observer.py extracts original compressed chunks from actual region/entity files with region/chunk/witness hashes and decodes native item/entity/marker data. Its output is ACTUAL_NATIVE_DISK_OBSERVATIONS_ONLY with UNKNOWN_NATIVE_PARTICIPANT_PERSISTENCE, null root/effect/save proof. It performs no world/NBT repair or item creation. The independent oracle redecodes the preserved bytes.

DComponentSaveCut and its test-only mixin observe/cancel a real EntityStorage.storeEntities call for the recipient entity chunk. It is armed only in the tagged fixture world and cannot be packaged into the release. Sender and recipient live in separate entity chunks. A saved baseline precedes the live transfer; the fault prevents recipient persistence. The actual write callback, disk distributions, witnessed SIGKILL, fresh process/container identities and 100-tick no-replay window are retained. Session/cargo authority is never reconstructed from counts or native files.

DObservedRestartGameTests separately observes native host save/reload boundaries and marker epochs. These are physical host executions, distinct from D10-CL01 client cases. Original-owner participant-save settlement remains a J05 blocker.

## Independent acceptance

component_oracle.py verifies actual native slots and item fingerprints, complete conservation/classified external deltas, identity lineage, permissions, bounded native movement and unchanged controls; actual native disk bytes; source/tree/JAR/fixture/driver/SDK/process identities; both players' original driver observations, menus and PNGs. native_oracle.py incorporates it into the cumulative 10-host-case schedule. verify.py reconciles actual XML and all 53 real-client case IDs; expected refusals remain separately counted. Five corrupt copies in test_native_oracle.py must reject acceptance. Model fixtures receive zero physical/client scenario credit.

The [frozen plan](D10-frozen-plan.json) and [stage report](D10.md) state the exact scope. Final evidence/pins are pending consolidated qualification. J02/J05 and D11 remain unexecuted.

# D05 API and observation boundary

`StorageCapabilities` and `StorageSnapshot` are pure Java under core/kernel/storage. `StorageCapabilities.evaluate` consumes immutable bounded facts and a native-item projection, checks supported kind, known/loaded/topology/protection/loot/lock/component/slot policy, and computes matching removal stock and compatible insertion capacity. Metadata limits are two participants, 27 slots each, 54 total, with unique participant/local-slot identity. Occupied stack limits and insertion limits are independent: a 16-stack probe cannot invalidate an unrelated valid full 64-stack, and an unstackable default item still obeys its native limit. A mismatched fingerprint cannot merge or fulfill another item. Unsupported, unknown and refused facts return zero quantities, never an apparent empty capacity.

`Item` identifies native registry ID, native codec fingerprint, maximum stack size and default/non-container status. `Slot` retains immutable participant/index, current item/count, occupied limit, probe insertion limit and separate insert/remove booleans. These are data projections, not capabilities. Language/client-created values cannot substitute for trusted native observations or authorize effects.

`StorageSnapshot.Visible` contains world/storage/generation/epoch/tick, stable native participant incarnation/marker generation, immutable slots and an inventory revision digest. It has no receipt ID, saveConfirmed, original-root or settlement field. `Unavailable.INSTANCE` is the single fieldless client-safe result for all missing/private/unknown/refused observations. A native live count does not imply journal/save confirmation.

`MinecraftStorageAdapter` requires ServerLevel, the existing StorageIncarnationAdapter, an immutable current metadata supplier, StorageAccessPolicy and explicit per-member Protection. It must execute on the server thread. `check(scope,id,operation,nativeProbe)` permits only INSPECT/DEPOSIT/WITHDRAW, verifies a current D03 decision and acknowledged registered native identity, and freshly rechecks identity/protection after bounded reads. Its Check is server-only observation data with a typed refusal and no quantities on refusal. DEPOSIT withholds matching withdrawal counts; WITHDRAW withholds insertion capacity. A Check is not an A permit or replayable receipt. J02 must obtain authority and re-observe at the same non-yielding effect boundary; D09 must additionally apply actual transfer source/destination policies.

`observe(scope,id)` requires a current INSPECT decision before returning actual slots. Deposit permission never implies inventory inspection. It validates all native items/slots and rechecks the decision, incarnation and protection after reading. No client-facing refusal includes hidden identity, label, counts, ACL, owner or private reason. Inventory revisions are computed from the ordered actual immutable slot facts and change with content; no inventory ledger or persistence owner is introduced.

ChestStorageAdapter requires exact `Blocks.CHEST` plus exact ChestBlockEntity class, and checks native lid obstruction. BarrelStorageAdapter requires exact `Blocks.BARREL` plus exact BarrelBlockEntity class. Both check loaded chunks before accessing state/entity. Double topology and participant identity come from the existing D02 owner; both canonical members are checked separately, with no repeated half. Each participant is checked for unresolved loot and isLocked before getItem; native observation does not unpack loot, open a menu or mutate inventory. Every slot consults actual canPlaceItem/canTakeItem and actual item/container limits. The removal observation uses the supported vanilla container's current policy; future transfer code must recheck the actual receiver as well.

Native item identity comes from BuiltInRegistries and the native ItemStack codec normalized to count one. SHA-256 is a fingerprint of that pinned native representation, not a receipt. Only empty component patches and non-container items are eligible. Nested inventory, bundle/projectile storage and EntityBlock items are refused. A non-default or unsupported stack anywhere in a supported container conservatively refuses the whole supported observation; no unknown slot is silently counted empty. Read/check methods have no setItem, removeItem, marker creation, chunk-load or Jobs calls.

The test-only DStorageAdaptersGameTests exercises native capacity/slots and refusal controls. DStorageObservationServer is installed only in the selected tagged-world client fixture, never the release or ordinary GameTest phases. It binds actual registered markers through the sole metadata owner, scopes observer commands from actual server players, and permits fixture mutations only from console. The production mod descriptor/mixins remain unchanged. DStorageObservationClient reuses the established genuine client driver; its D-owned wrapper keeps the established SDL offscreen renderer in two distinct native client containers. Independent verification requires actual multiplayer play, distinct container/process namespaces and the established native render environment, native packet/menu/observer agreement, authenticated principal matching, before/after state, privacy controls and native screenshot bytes.

The client fixture retains only its two fresh test-arena chunks before asynchronous metadata/marker setup, then reads those loaded containers. The production readers still check loaded state before access. Host-owned player bind directories are created before Docker startup. Public observer requests occur before opening the BEFORE menus; native menus remain visibly open across the barrel update. Native screenshots wait for their real container screen. The observer query and native menu keep independent incoming-packet evidence.

The renderer is the existing SDL offscreen software backend. Both clients remain full native Minecraft JVMs; actual multiplayer play, incoming synchronization, visible native container screens and rendered screenshots are mandatory. The configured and native-observed world seed must both equal 20261027. The actual server property hash and selected properties are retained before temporary world cleanup.

# D07 — Finite follow-player policy

Status: OWNED_GATES_PASS. The exact final candidate passed every mandatory cumulative gate. The measured final qualification is recorded below. Qualified [D06 predecessor](D06-handoff.json) retains exact source/docs/JAR/run/artifact pins. Design input: 37fbf49e2aec4eddb3c7600217e585a1b349e48f, prompt D07. Frozen cc.cd/1.0.0 bytes and 57 fixtures remain identical to source.

FollowPolicy owns a finite pure session: stable authenticated principal and actor generation, 2–4 block desired distance, 16 horizontal block initial range, 1200 tick deadline, 128 cumulative travel blocks, 8 loaded block lookahead, and at least 10 ticks between coordinate observations and repath proposals. Pausing consumes the original clock and at most 100 cumulative disconnected ticks. Resume cannot replenish allowances. Tighter owner limits persist. Missing current authority, competing owner, changed identity/dimension, death and unloaded terrain stop movement. STOP is provider independent and terminal sessions cannot restart.

FollowObservationAdapter uses public native navigation under an injected exclusive owner, registers no production hooks, and advances externally once per native tick. It reads player coordinates every 10 ticks, checks disconnect/dimension/liveness/control each tick, and stops only its own native path. Every accepted segment has at most 32 nodes and at most 8 blocks of actual path length; nodes must be safe and loaded. An interrupted tick stream fails closed. No actor teleport or chunk ticket is used. A/J02 must charge the same root and own custody/scheduler; J05 owns integrated restart/cancel settlement. A fresh server restart creates no automatic route.
