# D11 component handoff and production boundaries

This page freezes the independently qualified D component surface. D11 adds qualification readers and final gates. It adds no production composition or capability. The [cc.cd/1.0.0 ports](contracts/PORTS.md), [action rules](contracts/ACTION_SEMANTICS.md), [field dictionary](contracts/FIELD_DICTIONARY.md), and [semantic rules](contracts/semantic-rules.json) remain byte-identical to the external contract pin. Native objects never enter the pure core wire contract.

## Metadata schema, readers and migration

`core/.../storage/StorageMetadataCodec` implements `cc.storage-metadata/1`; `StorageMetadataStore.open/createNew` and `StorageRegistry` own metadata snapshots only. The exact format and operator recovery rules are in [METADATA_FORMAT.md](METADATA_FORMAT.md). The payload contains only schema, world_id, revision, records, assignments and bindings, wrapped in checksum_sha256/payload. It cannot contain stock, credits, Jobs, reservations or effect state. Stored records include full explicit ACLs; missing ACLs never become public.

Current/previous/pending/previous.pending snapshots and an OS lock establish one bounded metadata owner. Pending is never automatically promoted. Invalid current, unknown version/checksum/world, interrupted lineage or a second writer produce a read-only view while preserving originals. Valid current replacement can outlive an unreceived acknowledgement; an old expected revision cannot silently retry as a new write. Bounds include tombstones and stale references:4096 records,4096 assignments,32 grants,4 roles,8 MiB snapshots and a default32-write queue (hard maximum64). Replacement headroom is3×snapshot limit+65,536 bytes. IO occurs through the dedicated bounded metadata owner, without per-tick disk work.

Migration is an explicit future versioned operation. Stop the metadata owner through the qualified world lifecycle, preserve the complete metadata/native world/A save lineage, validate old/new readers and rollback compatibility, write a separate reviewed candidate, then reobserve bindings and grants. Unknown bytes remain intact. No D reader repairs files, widens grants, creates compensation items or proves effect recovery. A metadata restart acknowledgement never confirms both inventory participants or original-owner settlement.

## Exact component storage matrix

These are the actual test-registered component capabilities. Production marker installation and registration remain deferred to J01.

| Native kind | Exact eligible implementation | Members /slots | Orientation and observed boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Normal single chest | exact `ChestBlockEntity` class and `Blocks.CHEST` |1 /27 | N/S/E/W; loaded, unblocked, current marker and topology |
| Normal double chest | two exact normal chest instances; complementary LEFT/RIGHT states |2 /54 total | canonical member order; each physical half counted once; split/pair/replacement invalidates the old aggregate |
| Vanilla barrel | exact `BarrelBlockEntity` class and `Blocks.BARREL` |1 /27 | all six facings; opening is not topology replacement |
| Trapped chest, shulker, hopper, dispenser, dropper, furnace, modded chest subclass | outside the exact whitelist |refused | the frozen native campaign exercises all seven; no generic Container fallback |
| Ender chest and other unlisted endpoint types | outside the whitelist |unsupported | policy refusal; no extra native case credit is inferred for an unenumerated type |

An unloaded, locked, unresolved-loot, protected, malformed, stale or clone-quarantined container is unavailable, never empty. Checks precede every slot read that could unpack loot. Items require the installed registry ID plus the SHA-256 of the actual `ItemStack.CODEC` encoding of `copyWithCount(1)` through the current registry serialization context. Nondefault component patches and container/bundle/charged-projectile-bearing stacks refuse. Native slot maximum, insertion/removal policies and complete participant distributions determine capacity; names alone cannot select slots.

## Installed native seams and restrictions

| Actual D implementation | Allowed component operation | Production owner still required |
|---|---|---|
| `StorageRegistry`, `StorageAccessPolicy`, `StorageResolver`, `RecipientResolver` | bounded pure metadata, operation grants, stable visible endpoint resolution | J01/J04 authenticated ingress, server selection/confirmation, membership and real citizen control |
| `StorageIncarnationAdapter` and `StorageMarkerAccess` | PLAN /WRITE_MARKER /OBSERVE with server-thread authority, one current world owner and bounded8192 markers | J01 installation, lifecycle/retention association and coordinated rollback fencing |
| `MinecraftStorageAdapter`, `ChestStorageAdapter`, `BarrelStorageAdapter` | exact whitelist, read/check, live slot fingerprint/capacity/protection revalidation | J01/J02 current authority and installed protection integration |
| `MinecraftNavigationAdapter` | finite captured COME, stable storage/recipient routes and guarded native path suffix | J02 original-root actor ownership, remaining deadline/travel, leases and charging |
| `FollowObservationAdapter` | bind actual server player UUID, bounded observation/repath, STOP/pause/resume | J02 original owner, current root/generation and scheduler; no fresh allowance on resume |
| `MinecraftTransferAdapter` | exact native withdraw/deposit under current source/destination and disjoint cargo selection | J02 original-root resources/custody/effect and installed primitive requalification |
| `VillagerTransferAdapter` | explicit controlled carrier stock or exact pickup; stable enrolled recipient, one-use cargo and native reach | J02 custody, recipient consent/ownership and original effect settlement |

All native observations require the server thread and loaded native participants. No operation forces chunks, teleports an admitted actor or reads a player's inventory. Storage selection at J01 must use the actual authenticated server raycast, ≤6-block real interaction reach and ≤40-tick witness; selection alone creates no persistent marker. A/C textual UUIDs are candidates and cannot construct authority. This branch imports no peer C/A implementation.

COME/GO retain600 ticks,64 blocks,1.5-block arrival, ≤8 standing candidates,≤256 native nodes,≤121 loaded-chunk probes,≥10-tick repath and100-tick no-progress limits. FOLLOW retains1200 ticks,128 blocks,2..4-block target band,≤8 lookahead,10-tick observation/repath and100-tick disconnect pause within the original deadline. Delivery is one explicit default-component item,q1..64,≤8 batches; chest transfer reach3 blocks and native villager handoff reach2.5 blocks. Every existing50 ms p99/250 ms maximum component timing gate and unchanged D01 baseline comparison repeats on the final candidate. Smaller A remaining bounds always intersect these component ceilings.

## Native mixin and save-cut evidence

The fixture-only `parallel-d.mixins.json` selects `StorageMarkerMixin` against installed `net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity`. Its exact loadAdditional(ValueInput), saveAdditional(ValueOutput), preRemoveSideEffects(BlockPos,BlockState), setRemoved(), setBlockState(BlockState), setLevel(Level) and clearRemoved() descriptors are recorded by D11 from the installed Minecraft26.3 server JAR. Native break/rebuild/pair/split/clone/reload tests then execute those serialization/lifecycle hooks. The unchanged production descriptor never registers this marker mixin.

The separate test-only `DEntityChunkSaveMixin` targets `EntityStorage.storeEntities(ChunkEntities)` and its private final ServerLevel `level` field. It withholds an observed recipient entity-chunk write only in the explicitly tagged fault fixture. It never edits saved NBT or supplies a production save protocol. D11 retains actual server/native-class hashes and javap descriptors for BlockEntity, EntityStorage, SimpleContainer, NonNullList and AbstractVillager. J01 must requalify installation; J02 must reverify the actual transformed callback-free inventory primitive before activation.

Courier live/saved/restored6/7/2 differs from a partially persisted handoff live5/5 but saved/restored5/1. Actual native region bytes, fresh JVM/container identities and100 native read-only ticks witness UNKNOWN persistence and absence of automatic component replay. These are component observations, not A save proofs. Unknown saves cannot authorize replay or new source credit.

## Explicit deferred J adapters

| Gate /owner | Required integration and remaining acceptance |
|---|---|
| J01 | install marker mixin through qualified composition; authenticate registration/confirmation and6-block/40-tick native selection; associate one metadata owner with the real world and retention lifecycle; qualify restart/rollback and privacy/protection mapping |
| J02 | translate proposals to verified A10/I00 APIs; preserve original root/owner/generation, resource/actor leases, cumulative deadline/travel/scan budgets, exact effect/custody and follow/courier scheduling; requalify transformed native inventory primitives |
| J04 | connect production storage/beneficiary/citizen resolution and operation-specific admission without hidden-ID disclosure or explicit-to-nearest fallback |
| J05 | qualify actual save confirmation for every mutated participant and exact original effect/owner; reconcile ambiguous crash/restart/cancel without replay, foreign credit or fabricated settlement |
| J06 | merge D-only index/manifest fragments into the current shared documentation and run the complete repository documentation audit and integrated release gates |

Concrete A10/I00 adapter symbols are TO_VERIFY at J00. Neither historical A status nor B independent readiness proves integrated prerequisites. J00 requires separately qualified C08 and D11 handoffs, A10 and qualified A+B I00. This stage does not start J00 or activate production.

# D01 metadata API

Package: `dev.aivillages.core.kernel.storage`. No Minecraft/Fabric imports, native initializer, scheduler, inventory/effect/Job ledger or retention owner is added.

| Type/API | Contract |
|---|---|
| StorageRegistryLimits | Hard ceilings of 4096 records including tombstones, 4096 beneficiary-role keys, 32 grants/record, four purpose roles and an 8 MiB current snapshot. Custom limits can only tighten them. The write reserves three snapshot sizes plus 64 KiB of free replacement/rollback headroom. |
| StorageRegistry.Snapshot | Immutable world/revision, UUID-keyed records, separate beneficiary-role assignments and strict binding references. Binding metadata is never live native authority. |
| StorageRegistry.Record | World+storage UUID identity, NFC display label, owner, purpose roles, explicit ACL, revision/generation/ACL revision, state and finite adapter ID. Registration is PENDING_BIND. |
| StorageRegistry.Authority | Explicit pure server-adapter policy for caller/subject control and record operations. No permissive production default. It runs on the IO owner and must not call native game-thread objects. |
| registerMetadata | CAS on world revision, owner control and registration authority; returns a new stable UUID only after metadata acknowledgement. |
| rename / updateAcl / tombstone | CAS on world and record revisions plus operation-specific policy. Rename preserves identity/generation; ACL replacement requires grant and revoke authority; tombstone increments generation and retains the identity. |
| assignRole | Separate `(world, beneficiary, role)` map. Expected assignment revision -1 creates; a matching nonnegative revision explicitly reassigns. PUBLIC is not a beneficiary. Storage generation is checked at lookup; stale/tombstoned references do not resolve. |
| queryVisible / roleMetadata | Pure permitted metadata views. Lookup folds names without granting authority or choosing the first namesake. Neither method resolves physical inventory or grants access. |
| StorageMetadataStore.open | Returns a future; filesystem operations run on the bounded dedicated IO worker. Missing/corrupt/unsupported originals are preserved read-only, with a compatible previous snapshot used only as a diagnostic view. |
| StorageMetadataStore.createNew | Explicit future-based initialization of a new directory only. It never overwrites an existing directory or imports a legacy record permissively. |
| closeAsync | Returns immediately; queued mutations finish before lock/file closure on the IO worker. No caller-thread filesystem close or unbounded fallback queue. |
| Ack | ACKNOWLEDGED, REVISION_CONFLICT, DENIED, READ_ONLY, LIMIT, STORAGE_FULL, BUSY, INVALID or IO_ERROR, with revision and optional storage UUID. Successful reason is METADATA_ONLY_ACK; it is not an A receipt or Minecraft save proof. |
| StorageMetadataCodec | Strict canonical UTF-8 metadata schema/checksum and frozen cc.cd validation for records/assignments/binding references. Unknown fields, inventory/Job/credit data, missing ACLs and duplicate identities fail closed. |

NFC labels keep their display spelling. Lookup uses the pinned Unicode 16.0 default full case-fold C/F data, including expansions and non-ASCII special cases. The generated table and official source/license/provenance live in the D-owned source prefix; no new runtime dependency or version migration is introduced. Java 25's Unicode baseline is unchanged. The source digest is `6f1f9c588eb4a5c718d9e8f93b782685e5c7fec872cf05e8e6878053599e09bb`.

Records describe purpose roles; assignments describe beneficiary defaults. A shared or organization-owned chest can be a citizen's default while its owner and ACL remain unchanged. Names and metadata bytes never grant native access. D02 must establish/revalidate native bindings, D04 supplies access semantics, and J01/J02 supply actual authenticated ingress/lifecycle/A authority. The module remains inert until integration.

# D00 implemented API

Package: `dev.aivillages.core.kernel.storage.contract`. The domain layer imports no Minecraft, Fabric or Fabric-adapter classes. No entrypoint, scheduler, registry writer, Job/effect writer or world-authority factory is added to production.

| API | Observable contract |
|---|---|
| `StorageCodec.decode(String)` / `decode(byte[])` | Validate canonical UTF-8 cc.cd/1.0.0 envelope, exact schema, then frozen cross-field semantics. Return an immutable `StorageWire.Message`, or `StorageCodec.Invalid` with INVALID_SCHEMA/INVALID_SEMANTICS. Bytes must include exactly the canonical final LF. |
| `StorageCodec.encode(Message)` | Deterministic sorted-key compact JSON with one LF. Explicit null fields are preserved. |
| `StorageCodec.evaluate(Message, StorageWire.Context)` | Compare the projection with separate in-process observations and return VALID or REFUSED_EXPECTED. This performs no world observation, admission, resume, transfer or settlement. |
| `StorageWire.Message.kind()` / `body()` | Read-only kind and deeply immutable body, including nested maps/lists. A public message constructor is not exposed. |
| `StorageWire.Context` | Nullable contextual observations: trusted generation, requirement satisfaction, authenticated/question principals, current incarnation, current ACL revision, authenticated A-proof flag and eligible registered count. Never read this record from chat/wire input or treat it as a world-authority capability. |

The 17 envelope kinds are DialogueIntent, PlayerReplyIntent, AssistanceRequest, BlockerEvidence, StorageSelector, StorageRecord, PhysicalStorageBinding, StorageAccessDecision, ResolvedEndpoint, MobilityGoal, DeliveryGoal, CustodyCheckpoint, ActivityResumeSignal, VersionRevisionGeneration, SelectionWitness, StorageRoleAssignment and StageManifest. Their exact fields, variants, ranges and cross-field rules remain in the unchanged [field dictionary](contracts/FIELD_DICTIONARY.md), [schema](contracts/contract.schema.json), [ports](contracts/PORTS.md) and [semantic rules](contracts/semantic-rules.json).

Transport decoding is bounded to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes, depth 48 and 16,384 value/key tokens. Floating numbers, unsafe integers, duplicate keys, non-NFC strings, malformed UTF-8/surrogates, BOM, unknown fields/versions and noncanonical wire bytes are refused. Per-field limits are further restricted by the frozen schema. The embedded schema is checked against SHA-256 `99901b31634957fa8d1c3ebeaa668a5ab4297139a98a015bde81f7e5b89c6589` at class initialization.

VALID means the projection satisfies its structural/semantic/contextual checks. It grants no permission or physical truth. In particular, a decoded ALLOW or A-proof reference is not native authority. Only the deferred J adapter may supply actual authenticated ingress, effect-time observations and qualified A APIs. Context absence in a synthetic fixture is not authorization for a player action.

D00 does not implement metadata persistence, storage resolution, native binding, transfers, movement or conversational runtime behavior. D01 next implements registry metadata and bounded persistence within the same ownership boundary. J01/J02 install production registration/authority adapters later.

# Storage metadata format 1 and operator recovery

The format is independent of cc.cd/1.0.0 and A/B journals. Each world has one dedicated metadata directory and one OS file lock. The canonical UTF-8 current file is capped at 8 MiB, uses NFC strings, sorted keys, integer-only numbers and exactly one LF. Every record requires its complete frozen StorageRecord fields, including explicit ACL; each assignment requires complete StorageRoleAssignment fields. No quantity, reservation, Job, credit or effect state is admitted.

The outer object has exactly `checksum_sha256` and `payload`. The checksum is SHA-256 of the canonical payload bytes including their final LF. The payload has exactly `schema` (`cc.storage-metadata/1`), `world_id`, `revision`, `records`, `assignments` and `bindings`. Records are sorted by storage UUID; assignments by beneficiary kind/UUID/role; binding references by storage UUID. Duplicate storage IDs or beneficiary-role keys fail closed. Storage/assignment worlds must match the directory's expected server world. Assignment generations may remain stale after a tombstone, but stale references never resolve.

| File | Meaning |
|---|---|
| metadata.current.json | Current checksummed snapshot; only this metadata acknowledgement advances the caller's revision. |
| metadata.previous.json | Last valid current snapshot, staged/forced before replacing current. |
| metadata.pending.json | Uncommitted candidate, forced before replacement; ordinary open never promotes it. |
| metadata.previous.pending.json | Staged previous copy. An interrupted copy preserves all originals and requires operator reconciliation. |
| metadata.lock | OS ownership lock; a second owner opens read-only. |

A write checks current-file fingerprint and free replacement/rollback headroom, creates/forces pending, creates/forces the previous copy, atomically replaces previous, atomically replaces current, forces the directory, then acknowledges. Unsupported atomic move or force operations cause read-only failure rather than a weaker durability path. Queue overflow returns BUSY without caller-thread IO. Disk headroom failure returns STORAGE_FULL before touching snapshot files and can be retried after space returns. No identity or tombstone is evicted to make room.

An error makes the live owner read-only without claiming the candidate acknowledged. After a process kill, ordinary open accepts a fully valid current/previous lineage or remains read-only with all original files. A valid replacement may be visible even if the old caller never received acknowledgement; retry with an old expected revision conflicts. This is metadata atomicity, never item transfer, participant-save durability or original-owner settlement.

## Migration and coordinated rollback rules

1. Stop the metadata owner and use the qualified A/world maintenance lifecycle before changing files. Preserve byte-for-byte copies of the entire metadata directory, associated native world and actual A save lineage. Never edit live files under an active owner.
2. Inspect versions, checksums, world IDs, revisions, pending/previous files and the recorded native/A lineage. The normal opener never repairs, deletes, promotes pending, rewrites unknown formats or widens ACLs. A valid previous file is only a read-only diagnostic view when current is missing/corrupt/unsupported.
3. An unsupported version needs a separately versioned, reviewed migration with old/new fixtures, explicit owner/ACL policy and verified rollback compatibility. Missing ACL or owner fields remain untrusted; they must not become public/default grants. Preserve original unknown bytes while producing a separate reviewed candidate.
4. Coordinate any rollback with the actual native world and A participant-save history. Metadata-only rollback cannot establish identity continuity against a newer native marker/world. Generation counters are not proof against rolling both histories back. D02 must reobserve binding incarnations/topology after restart or rollback; J/A must qualify effects and custody.
5. Reopen a reviewed compatible current/previous set under the expected world, then explicitly revalidate native bindings and authorization before integration. Keep uncertain records unverified and preserve the archived originals. D01 offers no automatic recovery/promotion command and no inventory compensation.

J01 owns the real metadata directory/retention lifecycle adapter. D01 tests exercise temporary metadata files and real terminated JVMs only; they do not execute a Minecraft world or establish native save evidence.

DeliveryPolicy admits one eligible default-component item, quantity1..64, distinct authorized same-world/dimension endpoints and at most8 carrying batches. Same logical or overlapping physical endpoints refuse with zero transfer/credit. These-items admission requires a deliberate current source/participant/slot witness, actual native stack instance, exact selected components/count, matching principal and a lifetime<=40 ticks. Player inventory is never an implicit source. Pure observations distinguish READY, IN_FLIGHT, DELIVERED_LIVE, BLOCKED and UNCERTAIN; they contain no Jobs receipt or save authority.

The exact design input remains `37fbf49e2aec4eddb3c7600217e585a1b349e48f`, prompt D05. The cc.cd/1.0.0 manifest/schema and all 57 source/docs fixtures remain unchanged.

StorageCapabilities defines finite pure eligibility, independent per-slot occupied/insertion limits and native item fingerprints. StorageSnapshot defines immutable live facts with stable native participant identities, and one fieldless unavailable projection. MinecraftStorageAdapter provides current-loader read/check ports for exactly normal single chest, normal double chest and barrel. It requires the existing incarnation owner, immutable acknowledged metadata, current D03 access policy and explicit protection on every participant. ChestStorageAdapter and BarrelStorageAdapter test actual vanilla state and exact native class, so trapped-chest inheritance cannot expand support. See [D05_API.md](D05_API.md) and the [owned architecture/support matrix](D05_ARCHITECTURE.md).

Loot-table and lock checks precede every native slot read; no observation unpacks loot. Missing/unloaded/unknown/refused state cannot become an empty container. Default-component non-container stacks use native registry identity, SHA-256 of the native count-one codec projection, and actual item/container slot limits. Insertion/removal policies are consulted separately. Both double-chest participants are inspected once, with unique incarnation/local-slot pairs and combined capacity bounded to 54 slots. A native protection veto or invalid topology/components/slot policy refuses the whole observation. The adapters never alter native inventory, force chunks, open menus or create Jobs/receipts.

INSPECT alone permits exporting actual slots. A deposit-only check withholds withdrawal stock counts and a withdrawal-only check withholds insertion capacity. The separate client observer projection still requires INSPECT; denied/private/missing/deposit-only observer results are identical fieldless unavailable values. Private live facts, quantities and reasons never reach the unauthorized observer channel. This does not change vanilla player access.

## Frozen qualification plan

177 cumulative owned Java tests (18 new), 68 Python checks (seven new), five cumulative native cases (one new D05-GT01), and one genuine two-client case D05-CL01 are required on one exact candidate release.
